collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The village wants to hold its dance festival weeks after a sad death: go ahead, or wait until the family is ready.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The moon dance festival is in two days. But only last month, (friend)'s little brother drowned in the lagoon, and the whole village is still raw. (subject), who organizes the dance, does not know whether holding it would be cruel or kind. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) goes to (friend)'s family and asks. They talk for a long time. In the end, (friend) says (friend.his/her) brother loved the moon dance more than anything, and they should hold it. The family comes, and leaves early. Nobody minds.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) announces the festival will wait until the next moon. Some people are disappointed; some are relieved. (friend)'s family does not come to the next one either, and that is all right too. The dance goes on without them, and someone saves them a seat.
